cells.tense: You are following the direction you chose, long after the choosing itself ended.
cells.act: persist on your own reserves through the pressure
cells.ask: Take the hardest part of what's closing and sit with it on what you've got, then stop for the day — no borrowed energy, no good mood needed.
cells.core:
You picked a heading once and you're still walking it. The walking is the point now, not the pick. That's why you can hold what's heavy in this clearing without going down: the decision outlives the day you made it.

The finish will ask you to prove it every morning. You don't have to prove anything. Take the hardest part of what's closing, give it your own attention alone, with nothing borrowed — and then put it down and go do something else. Ground clears once the last thing moves. You don't force it. You keep showing up on your own feet, and that is what's actually carrying this to its end.
cells.sheetLine: You're still walking what you chose. Keep walking.
cells.verb: keep going on what you hoped for after the reasons to stop have piled up
cells.place: at the edge where one chapter closes so the next can start

cells.tense: You are bracing against an ending you've already decided will be ruin.
cells.act: write both sides of it on one page and close the page
cells.ask: Put both sides of the ending on one page — what it takes, what it opens — then close the page without choosing anything.
cells.core:
You've already written the ending that hasn't happened, and you wrote it as a wreck. The bracing runs faster than the clearing, so it does the clearing's work instead — sorting, guarding, rehearsing — and none of it touches the actual task, which is just to let the thing finish.

You know more than you're letting yourself say. Hold it a while before it leaves you. Take one page and put both sides down: what goes if this ends, what's possible if it ends. Then close the page. You don't have to choose. Weighing what you know before it's spoken is its own work, and it's been waiting for you. Rushing the timing doesn't speed the ending up; it only keeps you rehearsing it.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that already closed behind you.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Choose something still growing in your hands — a person, a plant, a body, a job — and give it steady, small, unforced care, nothing asked back.
cells.core:
Part of you is still at an old threshold, one hand on a knob that isn't there anymore. Attention keeps going back to what ended instead of forward to what's been cleared, and that backward pull costs more than the loss did. The strength you're known for hasn't left. It's just pointed at a room you can't get back into.

Care grows things without forcing them. Choose something still in your hands — a person, a plant, a body, a job — and look after it the way you'd look after something young. Small, steady, nothing demanded in return. You don't need to feel anything about it. The care itself fills you back up, not the other way round. That is how an empty seat gets its current again: not by pushing, but by tending.
cells.sheetLine: You're still at the old door. Something grows behind you.

cells.tense: You are holding up under weight other people would call impossible, and you call it normal.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Pick the load you've been hauling and carry it on purpose — noticing the weight as yours, not watching whether anyone sees you lift it.
cells.core:
You've stood under something heavy a long time, and your story about it is that it isn't heavy. Everything ran because you held it. You call that getting on. The people who lean on you have no reason to argue, and they don't.

The clearing stayed unfinished because you kept holding the pieces up instead of letting them fall where they'd fall. Carry your share by choice rather than by reflex. Notice the load as yours — its actual heft, not the version you report — and keep moving without watching for anyone to notice. A weight carried knowingly is carried differently, and it is finally yours to put down when you decide. What stays unnamed, waits; you've been waiting with it.
cells.sheetLine: You've carried it so well that no one knows it's heavy.
